our_argument_summary: S2 (12.00 hours) = exactly half a solar day; this is the dome's input (sun takes 24h to circuit), not a derived prediction. The dome's local sun at 5,733 km over 20,015 km disc produces a localized thermal+gravitational spike directly beneath the subsolar point, not the globally-symmetric two-bulge S2 pattern (Doodson 1921). The dome's own dashboard registers S2 as Predicted: 12.0 h | Observed: 12.0 h | Tolerance: 0.01% — a constant-equals-constant comparison at sub-noise tolerance. Verdict: Self-Contradicted.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 240 shows the dome's live-power dashboard entry for S2: 'Domain: S2 Solar Tidal Period — Predicted: 12.0 h | Observed: 12.0 h | Tolerance: 0.01% | Status: PASS — Source: NOAA CO-OPS'. Predicted and observed are both static constants by construction; the source label is decorative since the comparison never depends on a NOAA fetch (predicted equals observed numerically with no parameter).
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Hardcoded. SOLAR_H/2 = 24.00/2 = 12.0 vs Observed: 12.0 — algebraically identical. The 0.01% tolerance (0.0012 h, ~4 seconds) is below NOAA tidal measurement resolution and below any drift the comparison could observe.
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: Source: NOAA CO-OPS is window-dressing. No NOAA fetch determines the displayed Observed value; it is the rendered constant 12.0.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None. Current detail_verdict_text accurately cites raw-text/08-live-power.txt line 240 with verbatim values (12.0/12.0/0.01%).

code_analysis_tags.relabels_standard_evidence: S2 is the standard astronomical S2 lunar tidal constituent (Doodson 1921 classification); the dome doesn't dispute the period derivation or propose an alternative — it adopts the value and relabels the underlying mechanism as aetheric. The two-bulge geometric pattern that actually generates S2 is incompatible with dome geometry but the period itself is borrowed.
code_analysis_tags.post_hoc_evidence: S2 = 12.00 h is textbook tidal physics dating to Doodson 1921 (hyperlinked in detail_evidence). The dome adopted the value and timestamped 'Predicted: 12.0 h' against an Observed value it pre-set to the same constant. Part 3.1b 'trivial-transcription test' explicitly cited in detail_verdict_text.
code_analysis_tags.derives_from_dome_evidence: The dome's stated derivation 'SOLAR_H/2 = 24.00/2' is just dividing the solar day by 2 — algebraically equivalent to the standard derivation. No use of dome-specific parameters (disc_radius, firmament_height, sun altitude 5,733 km). The two-bulge spatial pattern the dome would need to derive in order to match the actual S2 phenomenon is GEOMETRICALLY EXCLUDED by dome parameters (Section 2.2).

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome's S2 entry uses correct astronomical taxonomy — S2 is indeed the principal solar semidiurnal tidal constituent (Doodson 1921 classification, hyperlinked in wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence). Naming this constituent and asserting its 12.00 h period is consistent with standard tidal physics.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Correct taxonomy is not prediction. The 12.00 h period is the algebraic consequence of the 24 h solar day divided by 2 (wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence: 'half a solar day') — and the solar day is the model INPUT (the dome's sun circuit period), not output. Additionally, the dome's spatial geometry (sun at 5,733 km over a 20,015 km disc, wins.json:WIN-046.detail_evidence) cannot produce the observed two-bulge S2 pattern (Section 2.2 of docs/index.html line 1084: 'Tidal Pattern: One Spike vs. Two Bulges'). And the dashboard registers Predicted=12.0/Observed=12.0/Tolerance=0.01% (raw-text/08-live-power.txt:240) — a constant-equals-constant comparison at sub-measurement tolerance, structurally null per Part 3.1b trivial-transcription test (wins.json:WIN-046.detail_verdict_text).

deeper_analysis:
Two-patch verification, both landed cleanly. The decider chose option (a) from c3 hole #1's recommendation set (structural-signature citation rather than option (b) propagate-WIN-045-audit-forward). Both options were valid; (a) is more concrete and reader-accessible. The replacement text drops the c3 phrase 'structural signature of a hardcoded validation' but preserves substance: 'constant-equals-constant comparison at 0.01% sub-noise tolerance' communicates the same architectural critique.

OTHER SIDE: A dome defender could argue the 0.01% tolerance citation actually HELPS them — 'our dashboard cleanly passes the prediction'. But the structural critique is exactly that passing-by-construction is methodologically null: the value is the input, the tolerance is below measurement resolution, and PASS is a foregone conclusion. The replacement language anticipates and defeats this rebuttal.

Three carry-over c3 holes (ISS-2553/2554/2555) remain open in the decider's queue. ISS-2553 (S2/S1 amplitude inversion) is the strongest among them — converts a spatial-only argument into spatial-plus-amplitude — and would benefit from analyst prose work. ISS-2554/2555 are minor stylistic improvements. Not re-flagging here; decider already has them.
